# Model in use does not update in Pi plugin

## Headline

The Worklog Pi extension footer (Line 3, right-aligned) shows a stale "model in use" after a mid-session model switch: the newly selected alias is paired with the previous session's resolved provider/model until the next Local Proxy response arrives — and permanently so when the switched-to model is not proxy-routed (e.g. a direct `deepseek` or `opencode` provider), because the `X-Resolved-Model` header never arrives. Intake RCA: `_resolvedModel` is never invalidated on `model_select` (only on `session_start`).

## Problem statement

After `/model` (or model cycling) mid-session, the footer's resolved provider/model does not update properly — it keeps showing the previously resolved model instead of the newly selected one. Root cause (confirmed by code reading): in `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/model-display.ts`, the resolved value (`_resolvedModel`) is only ever (a) set from the Local Proxy `X-Resolved-Model` response header in `after_provider_response`, or (b) reset to `null` on `session_start` (see WL-0MRZ1EIY5008VBE6). The `model_select` handler updates only `_selectedModel`. Two observable outcomes:

1. Immediately after a switch, the footer shows `newAlias → oldResolvedModel` (stale/misleading) until the first response carrying a new header arrives.
2. If the switched-to model is served by a non-proxy provider (`deepseek`, `opencode` in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`) no `X-Resolved-Model` header ever arrives, so the stale value persists for the rest of the session — or, if we only cleared the cache, the footer would show `(resolving)` forever, which is equally wrong.

## Users

- **Pi operator** switching models mid-session (e.g. `code` → `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`) to control cost/latency: needs the footer to reflect the switch immediately so they trust which model is actually serving the session.
  - *User story:* "When I run `/model` to switch to a cheaper or local model, I expect the footer to show the new model right away — not the old one — and definitely not forever."
- **Producer/auditor** reviewing recorded sessions: the displayed model must be trustworthy for RCA and cost attribution.
  - *User story:* "I check the footer to confirm which model handled a turn; a stale label makes the record unreliable."

## Acceptance Criteria

- When `model_select` fires mid-session (sources `set` and `cycle`), the previously resolved model is immediately invalidated: `getResolvedModel()` returns `null` right after the handler runs and the footer shows `<newAlias> → (resolving)` until a fresh proxy response arrives. Unit-testable in `model-display.test.ts` and a footer-render regression test in `session-health.test.ts`.
- When the selected model's provider is not the Local Proxy (no `X-Resolved-Model` header can arrive), the footer displays the model's own `provider/id` (e.g. `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`) instead of a stale proxy value or an unbounded `(resolving)` state. The proxy provider is identified by name (`Local Proxy`) — the same convention already centralised in `@worklog/shared/lease-release` (`LOCAL_PROVIDER_NAME`).
- Subsequent proxy responses update the resolved value exactly as today (header extraction, uppercase/lowercase handling, no-op on identical values, `onModelChange` firing) — no regression to existing behaviour covered by `model-display.test.ts`.
- The fix is fail-open when config is unavailable/unknown (no throw, no crash); existing `(resolving)`, right-alignment, and width-handling behaviour on Footer Line 3 (WL-0MRO7LWIX001516P, WL-0MSMDYJ3X00895MP, WL-0MSHENVKR002HZT5) is preserved.
- At least one unit test covers the end-to-end footer rendering for a mid-session switch (new alias + invalidation) and for the non-proxy provider case.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README (`packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — "Model/Provider Display (Line 3)" state table and the `model_select` event-row meaning), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Changes are confined to the Worklog Pi extension package (`packages/tui/extensions`); no local-proxy changes (the proxy already emits `x-resolved-model` on every response it routes — verified by the earlier spike SA-0MTYGZIWF000ZLU0 and a live probe).
- Must preserve the intermediate `(resolving)` state introduced by WL-0MRO7LWIX001516P and the session-start reset fix (WL-0MRZ1EIY5008VBE6) — this work is the mid-session analogue of that fix.
- Non-TUI modes must keep degrading gracefully (footer is a no-op outside TUI).
- Keep the fix surgical: no speculative refactor of the model-display module.

## Existing state

- `model-display.ts` (6222 B): module-level `_resolvedModel` / `_selectedModel`; `_onModelChange` is a **single callback slot** (multi-subscriber clobbering is a latent defect but not currently triggered). Listeners: `session_start` (resets `_resolvedModel`, seeds `_selectedModel` if unset), `model_select` (sets `_selectedModel` only), `after_provider_response` (sets `_resolvedModel` from `x-resolved-model`/`X-Resolved-Model` header only when it differs).
- `session-health.ts` (Line 3 render): `${selectedModel} → ${resolvedModel}`, else `alias → (resolving)`, else `resolvedModel`, else `—`. Subscribes via `onModelChange(() => tui.requestRender())` on first render.
- Pi SDK: `model_select` event carries `{ model: {provider, id}, previousModel, source: "set"|"cycle"|"restore" }` and fires on `/model`, model cycling, and session restore (verified in `pi-coding-agent` types `ModelSelectEvent` and `examples/extensions/model-status.ts`). `after_provider_response` exposes the raw HTTP response headers (lowercase-normalised).
- Proxy provider config lives in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`; the project already centralises the `Local Proxy` provider-name constant and models.json lookup in `packages/shared/src/lease-release.ts`.

## Desired change

1. In the `model_select` handler of `model-display.ts`: invalidate `_resolvedModel` (set `null`) and notify `_onModelChange` so the footer re-renders to `newAlias → (resolving)`.
2. If the newly selected model's provider is not the configured Local Proxy provider, treat the model's own `provider/id` as the resolved value immediately (no `(resolving)` limbo), so the footer shows the true model.
3. No change to the render logic in `session-health.ts` is expected (it already handles `null` resolved); add only regression tests. If a change becomes necessary it must keep the existing right-align and width-budget behaviour.
4. Update `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` to document the mid-session invalidation and the non-proxy fallback in the state table.

## Key Files:

- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/model-display.ts` — invalidate `_resolvedModel` on `model_select`; derive `provider/id` fallback for non-proxy providers.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/model-display.test.ts` — new tests: mid-session switch invalidation (all sources), non-proxy fallback, no regression to header extraction.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.test.ts` — footer Line 3 render regression test for mid-session switch and non-proxy provider.
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/session-health.ts` — verify only (render already null-aware); touch only if tests reveal otherwise.
- `packages/tui/extensions/README.md` — document updated `model_select` semantics and new fallback display.
- (reference, not changed) `packages/shared/src/lease-release.ts` — canonical `LOCAL_PROVIDER_NAME` convention to reuse.

## Related work

- WL-0MRZ1EIY5008VBE6 (completed) — Reset resolved model on session_start to avoid stale display across sessions. **Direct sibling:** same stale-display class; fixed at session boundary only, leaving the mid-session hole this item covers.
- WL-0MRO7LWIX001516P (completed) — Show model status in pi quickly; introduced the `(resolving)` intermediate state.
- WL-0MRDRZ32L00404D0 / WL-0MRF19R71004YJND (completed) — Session Health footer and the Line-3 model/provider line.
- WL-0MRC3F30E008XJN3 / WL-0MRC91VIN0089UXD / WL-0MRC3NOVZ000P0P5 (completed) — Model-display extension integration into the Worklog extension (status-line provenance).
- WL-0MSMDYJ3X00895MP, WL-0MSHENVKR002HZT5 (completed) — Line-3 right-alignment/truncation and alias/command position swaps that must not regress.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risks**
  - Header-based resolution remains the single source of truth for proxy-routed models; if a switch does not produce a new header (identical downstream model, request failure, non-proxy fallback routes), the footer can still lag. Mitigation: AC2 shows the selected model's own `provider/id` for non-proxy providers; `(resolving)` is the honest state while a proxy response is pending.
  - Some providers in `models.json` run under `modelOverrides` (e.g. `opencode`); deriving `${provider}/${id}` must use the *selected* model's provider/id, not overrides, to stay truthful.
  - Scope-creep risk: do not also "fix" the single-slot `onModelChange` (latent, no current trigger) or alias staleness on `session_start` guard (`! _selectedModel`) in this item — record as `discovered-from` follow-ups instead if the implementer confirms they are real.
- **Assumptions (documented, communicated on completion)**
  - A1. The observed defect is the stale resolved model after a mid-session switch, in both proxy and non-proxy scenarios (the only code path consistent with "does not update properly").
  - A2. The proxy provider is identified by the literal name `Local Proxy` (project convention in `lease-release.ts`); no config re-read is required if the check is by provider name against the constant, otherwise reuse the shared models.json lookup.
  - A3. On any mid-session `model_select` (including `restore`), invalidating the resolved value is correct; `session_start` already resets at session boundaries.
- **Open confirmation questions for the producer (non-blocking — see Appendix)**

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "What exactly did you observe when changing the model mid-session — did the left-hand alias update while the right-hand resolved model stayed on the previous one (or until the next turn), or did the whole label fail to change?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION** (recorded for producer confirmation). Research: the code only updates the resolved half from the `X-Resolved-Model` response header and invalidates it only on `session_start`, so the stale-resolved/lagging scenarios are the only code-consistent outcomes. Assumption A1 covers both.
- Q2: "When the switched-to model is NOT served by the Local Proxy (e.g. direct `deepseek`/`opencode` providers in `~/.pi/agent/models.json`), should the footer show the selected model's own `provider/id` (e.g. `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro`) instead of an endless `(resolving)`?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION — Recommended: yes** (shows the true serving model; `(resolving)` forever is untruthful). Assumption A2.
- Q3: "Should invalidating the resolved value also apply when the model is restored/re-selected at session start (`source: restore`), consistent with the WL-0MRZ1EIY5008VBE6 session-start reset?" — Answer: **OPEN QUESTION — Recommended: yes** (uniform behaviour; `session_start` already resets). Assumption A3.

  Research summary: pi's `model_select` events carry `model.provider`/`model.id` and `source` (`set|cycle|restore`); `after_provider_response` carries the raw HTTP headers and the Local Proxy adds `x-resolved-model` on the responses it routes (live-verified in spike SA-0MTYGZIWF000ZLU0). No new pi-version of the SDK contract is required.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MRC3NOVZ000P0P5** – Model display extension is not showing the provider (completed)
- **WL-0MRC91VIN0089UXD** – Move provider/model display to start of Worklog extension status line (completed)
- **WL-0MRE6JDT3004OSTF** – proactively release leases (completed)

### Repository file matches
Automated repo-file matches were reviewed and discarded as keyword noise (the full untruncated report is retained at `.worklog/tmp/find-related-full-WL-0MVGEB3IP002V8IB.md`). The high-signal related files are listed under **Key Files** above.
